# file:// Scheme — Local JSON Data Sources
#
# MyServer supports reading local JSON files directly via the file:// scheme.
# This is ideal for:
#   - Self-contained dashboards (no external dependencies)
#   - Data generated by cron jobs or other scripts
#   - Static catalogs, lists, or metrics
#   - Proving the dashboard works without network access
#
# Benefits over HTTP:
#   - No network round-trip (instant)
#   - No SSRF checks (not a network request)
#   - No authentication needed
#   - Hot-reloaded when the file changes

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# RULES
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# 1. Relative paths resolve against HOMEPAGE_CONFIG_DIR (default /app/config)
#    file://data/file.json     -> /app/config/data/file.json
#    file://scripts/status.json -> /app/config/scripts/status.json

# 2. Absolute paths work too:
#    file:///app/config/data/file.json

# 3. The file must contain valid JSON.

# 4. The file is read on every proxy request, but the PROXY caches the response
#    for 60s, so an edit shows up within about a minute.

# 5. The config watcher does NOT watch it. fsnotify is attached to the top of
#    the config directory only, and only for .yaml/.yml/.css/.js — so a JSON
#    file, and anything inside data/, produces no reload event at all. The
#    dashboard picks the new values up on its next poll (see 4), without the
#    page reloading itself.

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 1: Simple metrics file
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# config/data/metrics.json:
# {"cpu": 45.2, "memory": 82.1, "disk": 67.3}

widget:
  type: customapi
  url: file://data/metrics.json
  display: text
  mappings:
    field: cpu
    format: percent

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 2: Service status list
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# config/data/services.json:
# {
#   "services": [
#     {"name": "API", "status": "running", "url": "https://api.example.com"},
#     {"name": "DB", "status": "running", "url": "https://db.example.com"},
#     {"name": "Cache", "status": "degraded", "url": "https://cache.example.com"}
#   ]
# }

widget:
  type: customapi
  url: file://data/services.json
  display: dynamic-list
  mappings:
    items: services
    name: name
    label: status
    target: url

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 3: Release catalog
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# config/data/releases.json:
# {
#   "releases": [
#     {"title": "v2.1.0", "version": "stable", "url": "https://releases.example.com/v2.1.0"},
#     {"title": "v2.0.5", "version": "LTS", "url": "https://releases.example.com/v2.0.5"}
#   ]
# }

widget:
  type: customapi
  url: file://data/releases.json
  display: dynamic-list
  mappings:
    items: releases
    name: title
    label: version
    target: url

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 4: Monthly bandwidth (graph)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# config/data/bandwidth.json:
# {
#   "months": [
#     {"month": "Jan", "total_gb": 450},
#     {"month": "Feb", "total_gb": 380},
#     {"month": "Mar", "total_gb": 520}
#   ]
# }

widget:
  type: customapi
  url: file://data/bandwidth.json
  display: graph
  mappings:
    items: months
    name: month
    value: total_gb

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 5: Backup jobs status
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# config/data/backups.json:
# {
#   "jobs": [
#     {"name": "Database", "last_status": "success", "url": "https://backups.example.com/db"},
#     {"name": "Files", "last_status": "success", "url": "https://backups.example.com/files"},
#     {"name": "Config", "last_status": "failed", "url": "https://backups.example.com/config"}
#   ]
# }

widget:
  type: customapi
  url: file://data/backups.json
  display: dynamic-list
  mappings:
    items: jobs
    name: name
    label: last_status
    target: url

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 6: SSL certificate expiry
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# config/data/certs.json:
# {
#   "certificates": [
#     {"domain": "example.com", "days_remaining": 45, "url": "https://example.com"},
#     {"domain": "api.example.com", "days_remaining": 12, "url": "https://api.example.com"},
#     {"domain": "db.example.com", "days_remaining": 89, "url": "https://db.example.com"}
#   ]
# }

widget:
  type: customapi
  url: file://data/certs.json
  display: dynamic-list
  mappings:
    items: certificates
    name: domain
    label: days_remaining
    target: url

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 7: Docker container overview
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# config/data/docker.json:
# {
#   "containers": [
#     {"name": "nginx", "status": "running", "url": "https://nginx.example.com"},
#     {"name": "postgres", "status": "running", "url": "https://db.example.com"},
#     {"name": "redis", "status": "exited", "url": "https://cache.example.com"}
#   ]
# }

widget:
  type: customapi
  url: file://data/docker.json
  display: dynamic-list
  mappings:
    items: containers
    name: name
    label: status
    target: url

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 8: Storage pool usage
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# config/data/storage.json:
# {
#   "pools": [
#     {"name": "tank", "used_percent": 72, "url": "https://nas.example.com/tank"},
#     {"name": "backup", "used_percent": 45, "url": "https://nas.example.com/backup"},
#     {"name": "media", "used_percent": 91, "url": "https://nas.example.com/media"}
#   ]
# }

widget:
  type: customapi
  url: file://data/storage.json
  display: dynamic-list
  mappings:
    items: pools
    name: name
    label: used_percent
    target: url

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 9: Single value from nested JSON
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# config/data/system.json:
# {
#   "system": {
#     "cpu": {"usage": 45.2, "cores": 8},
#     "memory": {"used": 8589934592, "total": 17179869184},
#     "disk": {"used": 549755813888, "total": 1099511627776}
#   }
# }

widget:
  type: customapi
  url: file://data/system.json
  display: text
  mappings:
    field: system.cpu.usage
    format: percent

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 10: Top-level array
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# config/data/tasks.json:
# [
#   {"name": "Task A", "status": "done", "url": "https://tasks.example.com/1"},
#   {"name": "Task B", "status": "pending", "url": "https://tasks.example.com/2"}
# ]

widget:
  type: customapi
  url: file://data/tasks.json
  display: dynamic-list
  mappings:
    items: ""          # empty string = top-level array
    name: name
    label: status
    target: url

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# GENERATING JSON FILES WITH SCRIPTS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# You can generate these JSON files with cron jobs or scripts:

# config/scripts/generate-metrics.sh:
# #!/bin/bash
# cat > /app/config/data/metrics.json <<EOF
# {"cpu": $(cat /proc/loadavg | awk '{print $1}'), "memory": 82.1, "disk": 67.3}
# EOF

# Then add a cron job on the host:
# */5 * * * * /srv/myserver/config/scripts/generate-metrics.sh

# Or trigger from a MyServer script card:
# scripts:
#   refresh-metrics:
#     command: generate-metrics.sh
#     description: "Refresh local metrics"
#     timeout: 10
#     icon: mdi:refresh
